correctness.rationale: The supremum γ(s,x)=sup_{u>=0,||u||≤1}|s+<x,u>| equals max(|s+||x_+|||,|s-||x_-|||), a continuous seminorm bounded by √2||(s,x)||_2. Thus Nβ²=||(s,x)||²+βγ² is a complete norm with 1≤Nβ/||·||_2≤√(1+2β), permitting arbitrarily small distortion β>0. Convexity of γ² plus Hilbert parallelogram proves the 2-uniform-convexity modulus δ(ε)≥ε²/[8(1+2β)]; Browder–Göhde–Kirk provides the bounded-set fixed-point property. The fixed positive affine slice C={s,x>=0:s+<w,x>=1}, w_j=2^(-j), is unbounded via (0,2^j e_j). For p=(1,0), any y=(b,v)≠p has d_y=1-b>0. If z_n=(s_n,x_n) in G_C(p,y) escapes, then ||x_n||=r_n→∞, g_n=x_n/r_n weakly→0 by coordinatewise x_n,j≤1/w_j. The explicit norm-one support functional at z_n-p has F_n(p-y)→βd_y/√(1+β)>0, contradicting Nβ(z_n-y)≤Nβ(z_n-p). So every G_C(p,y) is bounded; Kirk–Ray localization applies for every nonexpansive C→C, giving a fixed point. Independently checked the support limit for escaping points j=15,20,25 and β=.037. The argument relies on exact strict β>0; at β=0 Hilbert Ray theorem forbids the conclusion.
